name: Huang Tengqi
profile: Listed on the Hurun China 2010 rich list (approx. US$150m) as founder of Xinlianxin Group (黄腾其), with interests in supermarkets, agricultural cultivation and property investment. No further public information could be verified in English or Chinese web searches.

name: Mayur Mukundlal Desai
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2018 (approx. US$144m) with wealth from Infibeam Avenues, the Ahmedabad fintech/e-commerce company behind the CCAvenue payment gateway. Infibeam's March 2019 shareholding filing lists 'Mayur Mukundlal Desai' as a public shareholder holding more than 1%. Not a director or executive of the company.
interesting_fact: Appears in Infibeam Avenues' official March 2019 shareholding pattern among public shareholders owning more than 1% of the company.
notes: Passive investor in Infibeam rather than founder (founders are Vishal Mehta and Vishwas Patel). No public profile found; identity beyond the shareholding filing unverified. Company was renamed AvenuesAI in 2025-26.

name: Rita Kishore Sinha
current_role: Non-Executive Director, SIS Limited (Security and Intelligence Services India)
profile: Rita Kishore Sinha is a long-time director and major shareholder (~16%) of SIS Ltd, the Patna-founded security, facility-management and cash-logistics group started by her husband, journalist-turned-politician RK Sinha. SIS is now one of India's largest private employers, with FY2026 revenue of about ₹15,982 crore; her son Rituraj Sinha is Group MD.
interesting_fact: SIS grew from a small Patna security agency into a multinational group; the company says revenue rose from ₹25 crore in 2002 to ₹15,982 crore in FY2026, with operations including Australia (MSS) and a cash-logistics JV with Prosegur.
deep_cut_fact: She is a lawyer by training: she holds a BA in Hindi and an LLB from Ranchi University, has around 32 years of legal experience and is enrolled with the Supreme Court Bar Association.
notes: Low personal media profile; the public face of SIS is son Rituraj Kishore Sinha (Group MD). Best route is SIS media relations.

name: Zhou Xiaodi
profile: Listed on the Hurun China rich list 2005-2007 (approx. US$130m) as head of Zhoushi Group (周小弟, 周氏集团), a real-estate developer. No further verifiable public information was found in English or Chinese searches.
notes: Very low footprint; last rich-list appearance 2007. Region and current status of the company unknown. Would need Chinese corporate registry research; not a strong podcast lead.

name: Rene R. Joyce
current_role: Director, Targa Resources Corp. (NYSE: TRGP); founding CEO (2005-2011)
profile: Rene Joyce is the founding CEO of Targa Resources, the Houston midstream natural-gas and NGL company he led from its 2005 formation until 2011, then served as executive chairman (2012-2014) and remains a director. Earlier he ran Tejas Gas pipeline subsidiaries and Shell's Coral Energy units, and has sat on the boards of Apache and Core Labs.
interesting_fact: Targa, which he built from a 2005 private-equity-backed startup, is now one of North America's largest independent midstream companies; in 2026 it signed 20-year integrated midstream agreements with ExxonMobil in the Permian Delaware Basin.
deep_cut_fact: He is both an engineer and a lawyer: BS in mechanical engineering from LSU (1970) and a JD from Loyola University New Orleans (1974); he sits on the LSU Foundation National Board and is a member of LSU's Society for Engineering Excellence.
notes: Highly relevant to energy theme (natural gas midstream, Permian). Low personal media profile; route via Targa corporate/investor relations or LSU engineering network. A Targa proxy noted a planned board retirement at an annual meeting—confirm current board status in latest proxy.

name: Rashmita Patnaik
current_role: Director/promoter, Falcon Marine Exports Ltd (Bhubaneswar, Odisha)
profile: Rashmita Patnaik is a long-serving director and promoter of Falcon Marine Exports, a Bhubaneswar-based seafood (mainly shrimp) processor and exporter founded in 1986 by Tara Ranjan and Prava Ranjan Patnaik. She also holds directorships in group companies such as Falcon Drinks, Falcon Real Estate and Falcon Holdings. Listed on Hurun India 2018-2019 (~US$120m).
interesting_fact: Falcon Marine Exports, set up in Odisha in 1986, grew into one of India's leading shrimp exporters and has been recognised in MPEDA's export awards (2018-19 awardee list).
notes: Non-executive, very private; company's public face is chairman Tara Ranjan Patnaik (Priyanka Mohanty named Joint MD in 2026). Board data from third-party MCA aggregators (qorpiq.com). No published company email found on falconmarine.in.

name: Ravinder Kumar Agarwal
current_role: Possibly Managing Director, Ravi Foods Pvt Ltd (Dukes India) — unconfirmed link to 'Singhania Foods International'
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2019 (~US$120m) in food & beverages under 'Singhania Foods International', a company name that could not be found online. The most prominent match is Ravinder Agarwal, MD of Ravi Foods Pvt Ltd (Dukes brand biscuits, wafers, confectionery), which says it runs 17 plants with ~5,000 staff; the identity link is unverified.

notes: Identity ambiguous: several Ravinder/Ravindra Kumar Agarwals exist (e.g. one at Suryajyoti Spinning Mills). Contact listed is Dukes' general email and only relevant if he is the Dukes MD — verify before outreach.

name: Jean-Marie Mognetti
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, CoinShares PLC (Nasdaq: CSHR)
profile: French-born Jean-Marie Mognetti co-founded CoinShares, Europe's largest digital-asset manager, which launched the world's first regulated Bitcoin ETP in 2015 and holds ~34% EMEA crypto-ETP market share. A former quantitative commodity trader, he has led the Jersey-registered firm since 2014, including its 2024 acquisition of Valkyrie and its move to a US listing.
interesting_fact: CoinShares launched the world's first regulated Bitcoin exchange-traded product in 2015—roughly a decade before US spot Bitcoin ETFs were approved.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he was a quant commodity trader at Hermes Commodities Fund Managers, after a Master's in Mathematical Trading and Finance from Sir John Cass Business School; Blockworks reports oil-industry/JPMorgan veterans Danny Masters and Russell Newton brought him into what became CoinShares in 2012.
notes: Frequent conference speaker and media guest — good podcast fit (bitcoin mining/energy angle via CoinShares' mining research and ETPs). Background story: blockworks.co 'Gone Crypto: Mognetti and the Birth of CoinShares'.

name: Anand Parekh
current_role: Founder and CEO, Alyeska Investment Group (Chicago hedge fund)
profile: Anand Parekh founded Chicago-based multi-manager hedge fund Alyeska Investment Group in 2007 after serving as a partner at Citadel, where he built and ran the Global Equities and Reinsurance businesses; earlier he was an MD at Deutsche Bank. His SEC 10%-owner filings in FrontView REIT and Strawberry Fields REIT reflect Alyeska fund holdings, not operating roles.
interesting_fact: Reuters reported in 2007 that the ex-Citadel equities head was launching Alyeska with about $1.5 billion of backing from Deutsche Bank—an unusually large seed for a debut fund.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a quant-minded hedge fund founder, he holds a BS in both Mathematics and English Literature from the University of Michigan.

public_contacts.value: https://www.alyeskagroup.com/ (Alyeska Investment Group, 77 W Wacker Dr, Chicago — firm office)

notes: Very low-profile hedge fund manager; Alyeska's site is a bare address page. Has appeared as a speaker for Bessemer Trust. Not to be confused with Dr. Anand Parekh (health policy). Name in SEC filings: Anand Christopher Parekh.

name: Stefano Caroti
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Deckers Brands (NYSE: DECK)
profile: Stefano Caroti became CEO of Deckers Brands (HOKA, UGG, Teva) in August 2024, succeeding Dave Powers. He joined Deckers in 2015 as President of Omni-Channel, then served as Chief Commercial Officer and interim HOKA president during the brand's breakout growth. Before that he was CCO/MD at PUMA (2008-2014) and spent years in senior roles at Nike.
interesting_fact: He personally ran HOKA as interim president (2022-2024) during the running brand's surge, before taking the top job at Deckers.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his Nike career he ran the company's Italian and German subsidiaries before taking over footwear and then retail for all of Europe, Middle East and Africa; he earned his undergraduate degree at Middlebury College in Vermont.
notes: Consumer/footwear CEO, so weak fit for energy/data-center themes; possible entrepreneurship angle via HOKA's scaling story. Name appears in SEC data as 'Caroti Stefano'.
